SECTION 6.08. Restricted Payments; Certain Payments of Indebtedness .

(a) No Loan Party will, nor will it permit any Restricted Subsidiary to, declare or make, or agree to declare or make, directly or indirectly,
any Restricted Payment, or incur any obligation (contingent or otherwise) to do so, except (i) each of the Borrowers may declare and pay dividends with respect to its common stock payable solely in additional shares of its common stock, and,
with respect to its preferred stock, payable solely in additional shares of such preferred stock (to the extent permitted to be issued hereunder) or in shares of its common stock, (ii) Restricted Subsidiaries may declare and pay dividends
ratably with respect to their Equity Interests, (iii) the Loan Parties may make Restricted Payments, pursuant to and in accordance with stock option plans or other benefit plans for management or employees of the Loan Parties and their
Restricted Subsidiaries, (iv) other Restricted Payments in an amount not to exceed the Available Amount immediately prior to the time of the making of such Restricted Payment, so long as at the time of making such Restricted Payment and
immediately after giving effect (including giving effect on a pro forma basis) thereto, (x) no Event of Default then exists or would result therefrom and (y) the Total Net Leverage Ratio is not greater than the ratio that is 0.5 to 1.00
lower than the maximum Total Net Leverage Ratio permitted under Section 6.12, and (v) the Company may make distributions and pay dividends to its equityholders, in each case, not otherwise permitted to be made by this Section 6.08 in
an aggregate amount not to exceed $10,000,000 during any fiscal year of the Company so long as, in each case, all of the following conditions are satisfied: (x) no Default shall exist immediately prior to or immediately after giving effect to
the distribution or dividend, and (y) after giving effect to such Restricted Payment and any Indebtedness incurred or assumed in connection therewith, on a pro forma basis, the Company is in compliance with the covenants set forth in
Section 6.12 (without giving effect to any applicable Total Net Leverage Ratio Adjustment); provided that any Restricted Payment made in reliance on this clause (v) shall not be included in the foregoing dollar limitation if, after
giving effect to such Restricted Payment and any Indebtedness incurred or assumed in connection therewith (including on a pro forma basis), the Total Net Leverage Ratio is not greater than the ratio that is 0.5 to 1.00 lower than the maximum Total
Net Leverage Ratio permitted under Section 6.12.

(b) No Loan Party will, nor will it permit any Restricted Subsidiary to, make or agree to
pay or make, directly or indirectly, any payment or other distribution (whether in cash, securities or other property) of or in respect of principal of or interest on any Indebtedness, or any payment or other distribution (whether in cash,
securities or other property), including any sinking fund or similar deposit, on account of the purchase, redemption, retirement, acquisition, cancellation or termination of any Indebtedness, except:

(i) payment of Indebtedness created under the Loan Documents;

(ii) payment of regularly scheduled interest and principal payments as and when due in respect of any Indebtedness permitted
under Section 6.01, other than payments in respect of the Subordinated Indebtedness prohibited by the subordination provisions thereof;

(iii) refinancings of Indebtedness to the extent permitted by Section 6.01; and

(iv) payment of secured Indebtedness that becomes due as a result of the voluntary sale or transfer of the property or assets
securing such Indebtedness to the extent such sale or transfer is permitted by the terms of Section 6.05.

findings.proposedIrEvidence: definitions[0] ('Total Net Leverage Ratio') numerator.right = MIN(Unrestricted Cash, MONEY 25,000,000 USD), with that $25,000,000 operand's provenance excerpt field set to null and sourceNodeKey null, yet the definition's overall sufficiency is marked 'COMPLETE'
findings.verifierReasoning: The proposed IR asserts a fully-specified formula for Total Net Leverage Ratio - including a specific $25,000,000 cap on the amount of Unrestricted Cash that may be netted against Total Indebtedness - and marks this definition COMPLETE, i.e. asserts full confidence. But no source text for this definition was ever retrieved (context bundle is empty) and the provenance for the $25,000,000 figure itself has no excerpt at all. The deterministic pass independently flagged this exact figure as IR_ONLY with no matching source-side figure. This ratio (Total Net Leverage Ratio) is the operative gate for the Available Amount basket (r4) and the uncapped-carve-out proviso (r6) in 6.08(a); if the true cash-netting cap differs from $25,000,000 (or does not exist at all), the leverage-ratio comparisons used to determine whether those baskets are available would be computed incorrectly, which could change a real compliance conclusion. Marking this COMPLETE despite having no retrievable source support is exactly the confident-but-unverifiable pattern that warrants the highest scrutiny.

findings.sourceEvidence: "No Loan Party will, nor will it permit any Restricted Subsidiary to, declare or make, or agree to declare or make, directly or indirectly, any Restricted Payment, or incur any obligation (contingent or otherwise) to do so, except (i) ... (v) ..."
findings.proposedIrEvidence: Rules r1-r6 (sourceSectionRef 6.08(a)(i) through (a)(v) proviso) are all encoded as standalone PERMISSION rules with sufficiency COMPLETE; no rule in the proposed IR carries posture PROHIBITION for the 6.08(a) default-deny clause, in contrast to 6.08(b) which is explicitly represented as rule ir-rule:d40c974c85b83963692a76ef (posture PROHIBITION) with exceptions (i)-(iv) attached to it.
findings.verifierReasoning: Section 6.08(a) is structured as a default prohibition on all Restricted Payments, with clauses (i)-(v) being the exhaustive list of carve-outs from that default prohibition. The proposed IR faithfully mirrors this structure for 6.08(b) (an explicit PROHIBITION rule r7 with four attached PERMISSION exceptions), but for 6.08(a) it only encodes the exceptions themselves as freestanding PERMISSION rules and never represents the governing prohibition. A Restricted Payment that does not fit any of (i)-(v) is, per the source, prohibited - but nothing in the proposed IR captures that default-deny posture for 6.08(a), so a downstream consumer relying on this IR could fail to recognize that any Restricted Payment outside r1-r6 is forbidden, rather than merely unaddressed.

findings.sourceEvidence: "No Loan Party will, nor will it permit any Restricted Subsidiary to, declare or make... any Restricted Payment... except... (iv) other Restricted Payments in an amount not to exceed the Available Amount..." (6.08(a) chapeau + (iv)); "No Loan Party will, nor will it permit any Restricted Subsidiary to, make or agree to pay or make... any payment... except: (i) payment of Indebtedness created under the Loan Documents..." (6.08(b) chapeau + (i)-(iv))
findings.proposedIrEvidence: ir-rule:4194826764240b0f44a6b546 (6.08(a)(iv)) and ir-rule:d40c974c85b83963692a76ef / 4f754763b38bddef4ecaaa2b / 2f5e10595a6a4fe8dfd7f90d / 3b23b140cedac1cfd49f04fe / f8199c767194cb7519f75729 (all under 6.08(b)) each set entityScope to only ["LOAN_PARTY"], with entityScopeExcluded empty.
findings.verifierReasoning: Both the 6.08(a) and 6.08(b) chapeaus bind Restricted Subsidiaries directly (via the 'nor will it permit any Restricted Subsidiary to' construction, which in standard drafting means the Restricted Subsidiary itself is restricted from performing the act, not merely that the Loan Party is restricted from permitting it), yet clause (iv) of (a) never names an entity (unlike (i)-(iii) and (v), which explicitly say 'the Borrowers', 'Restricted Subsidiaries', or 'the Loan Parties'), and none of clauses (b)(i)-(iv) name an entity either. Scoping all of these exceptions/prohibitions to LOAN_PARTY only, and omitting RESTRICTED_SUBSIDIARY from entityScope, could understate which entities are bound by the 6.08(b) prohibition and which entities may rely on the (a)(iv) Available Amount basket or the 6.08(b) exceptions, potentially producing a wrong permission/prohibition conclusion for a transaction undertaken by a Restricted Subsidiary rather than a Loan Party. I flag this as uncertain rather than definitively wrong because the source's silence on entity for these specific clauses is itself ambiguous.

findings.sourceEvidence: "...so long as, in each case, all of the following conditions are satisfied: (x) no Default shall exist immediately prior to or immediately after giving effect to the distribution or dividend, and (y) ...; provided that any Restricted Payment made in reliance on this clause (v) shall not be included in the foregoing dollar limitation if..."
findings.proposedIrEvidence: ir-rule:51de67c5055548ffb8f90dac (the proviso) lists only one condition (the leverage-ratio test) and relates to r5 solely via a dependsOn entry of relationshipType 'REQUIRES' with a free-text description characterizing the relationship as a cap-exclusion, rather than explicitly carrying forward r5's condition[1] ('no Default shall exist...').
findings.verifierReasoning: The source proviso only removes the $10,000,000 dollar limitation when its own ratio test is met; it does not, on its face, waive condition (x) (no Default) which independently governs all clause (v) payments. The proposed IR's r6 does not explicitly restate the no-Default condition, instead relying on an ambiguous 'REQUIRES' dependency pointing at r5. Depending on how a downstream system interprets that dependency, it could either correctly treat no-Default as still required, or incorrectly treat r6 as available even when a Default exists (since r6's own conditions array only contains the ratio test). This is not clearly wrong, but the encoding does not unambiguously preserve the source's surviving condition.

findings.proposedIrEvidence: The deterministic pass reported '0.5 RATIO does not appear as a RATIO value anywhere in the compiled IR' (twice); however, the value is in fact present at ir-expr:9cb48825d9b1686b3d9254ef (kind RATIO, value 0.5) and ir-expr:05887317f5df950450cb55b7, nested inside SUBTRACT/COMPARE 'attemptedStructure' nodes that the IR itself marks UNSUPPORTED/requiredReview because the Section 6.12(b) numeric ceiling could not be retrieved.
findings.verifierReasoning: On independent inspection, the 0.5 differential from the source is actually captured in the IR (twice), just nested inside a malformed/unresolved expression tree rather than as a clean top-level RATIO node, which appears to be why the deterministic scanner missed it. The genuinely missing piece - the numeric maximum Total Net Leverage Ratio under Section 6.12(b) - is already honestly disclosed by the IR itself (sufficiency PARTIAL, requiredReview true, explicit narrative explaining the truncated retrieval). I therefore do not think this deterministic signal points to an additional hidden omission beyond what is already transparently flagged, so I rate it non-material.
